description: Per-translation glossary overlay for the Wheel of Heaven Translation of Numbers (canon-cited chapters: 18, 21, 33). v1.0.0 (2026-11-01, Torah wave T1 Editor pass) carries the shared Torah conventions, identical in substance to the exodus-woh and deuteronomy-woh overlays (proper names, quotation marks, MT baseline / Ketiv-Qere / accents, Elohim referent and article, nefesh scope, 'the Testimony'), and the Numbers-specific decisions: zār 'outsider', the ḥērem vocabulary, the fiery serpent of Num 21, the priestly-dues vocabulary of Num 18 and the cult objects of Num 33:52. Cross-corpus decisions of the wave (tərûmâ 'oblation' with hērîm 'set apart'; nəḥōšeṯ 'bronze'; tôrâ 'law'; taḇnîṯ 'pattern') are proposed for the central glossary in exodus-woh/wave-t1-central-diff.json. Sign-off corrections (2026-11-01): reviewer fixes applied (elohim-referent rationale at Deut 4:7; KJV attribution of the canon's English; ḥērem Hiphil 'devote ... to destruction' in numbers-woh; bārāʾ 'create' outside Genesis and the published Exodus name forms ratified). Signed off at human review on 2026-11-01 (zarazinsfuss); this wave's central proposals were applied as central glossary v2.84.0, and the sign-off merge is v2.90.0. v1.1.0 (2026-11-02, Wave MC, Hebrew part (Num 11; Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5)): Num 11 added. The shared Torah conventions keep their text and gain the Num 11 refIds in appliesTo; new Numbers-specific entries ruach-spirit-on-the-elders-numbers-11 (lower-case 'spirit' for the rûaḥ apportioned to the seventy elders; the Kings transliteration is not extended to the Torah) and lexical-cruxes-numbers-11 (11:28 'from his youth' with the MT vocalisation; 11:8 'fresh oil'; the tiqqun at 11:15; the new name Tav'erah, to be added to the Torah name table at its next extension). Central proposals in leviticus-woh/wave-mc-he-central-diff.json. Wave MC signed off at human review on 2026-11-02 (zarazinsfuss); its central proposals were applied as central glossary v2.91.0 (New Testament), v2.92.0 (Septuagint) and v2.93.0 (Hebrew).

entries.source: (proper names and toponyms of the Torah narrative)
entries.lemma: Hebrew personal names, toponyms and gentilics in the Torah volumes of the Wheel of Heaven Translation
entries.partOfSpeech: Presentation convention for proper names in exodus-woh, numbers-woh and deuteronomy-woh (shared Torah convention, identical in the three overlays)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV/KJV English forms (Moses, Aaron, Egypt, Hormah, Sihon, Heshbon, Jordan, Jericho, Kadesh, Baal-peor)
entries.wohChoice: Transliterated Hebrew forms, as in genesis-woh and the signed-off exodus-woh chapters, with two grandfathered English exceptions, 'Moses' and 'Pharaoh'. Spelling rules: tz for tsade (Baal-Tzefon, Etzyon-Gever, Tzin, Tzalmonah, Betzer, Chatzerot, Rimmon-Peretz), except the country name 'Mitsrayim', which keeps the ts of the central `mitsrayim` entry and of the 119 occurrences already printed in genesis-woh and exodus-woh; q for qof (Qadesh, Qivrot-haTa'avah, Qehelatah, Mitqah, Yabboq); ch for chet (Chormah, Cheshbon, Chermon, Chor-haGidgad, Chashmonah); v for undageshed bet (Avihu, Ovot, Nevo, Avarim, Medeva, Livnah, Avronah); f for undageshed pe (Sufah, Nofach, Shefer, Dofqah); the article as 'ha' joined to the name (Pi-haChirot, Qivrot-haTa'avah, Beit-haYeshimot, Avel-haShittim, Iyye-ha'Avarim); 'Baal-' without apostrophe in compound toponyms (Baal-Tzefon, published at Ex 14:2, 9; Baal-Pe'or, Deut 4:3). Kept in their familiar English form: Moses, Pharaoh, Moab, Edom, Ammon, Sinai, Horeb, Marah, Elim, Sin, Arad, Arnon, Bashan, Og, Golan, the Negev, Mount Hor, Pisgah. Gentilics: English collective plurals for the peoples of the land (the Canaanite, the Amorite(s), the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, the Jebusite, as exodus-woh 3:8; the Levites; the Gadites); English '-ite' on the transliterated stem otherwise (the Re'uvenites, the Menashites). Mitsrayim / the Egyptians: 'Mitsrayim' for the country and the state; 'the Egyptians' where miṣrayim denotes the population as the agent or experiencer (exodus-woh 3:9 and Ex 14 passim; Num 33:3-4). Aetiological names are glossed in parentheses only where the Hebrew states the etymology in a causal clause (exodus-woh 17:7 'Massah (Testing)'); names whose wordplay is implicit (Chormah, Num 21:3; Be'er, Num 21:16, where the text adds 'that is the well') are left unglossed and the wordplay is given in commentary. Equivalence table (WoH = ASV): Nadav = Nadab; Avihu = Abihu; Chur = Hur; Yehoshua = Joshua; Aharon = Aaron; Yisra'el = Israel; Avraham = Abraham; Yitzchaq = Isaac; Ya'aqov = Jacob; Levi = Levi; Chormah = Hormah; Atarim = Atharim; Ovot = Oboth; Iyye-ha'Avarim = Iye-abarim; Iyyim = Iim; Zered = Zered; Vahev = Vaheb; Sufah = Suphah; Ar = Ar; Be'er = Beer; Mattanah = Mattanah; Nachali'el = Nahaliel; Bamot = Bamoth; Sichon = Sihon; Yahatz = Jahaz; Yabboq = Jabbok; Cheshbon = Heshbon; Kemosh = Chemosh; Dibon = Dibon; Nofach = Nophah; Medeva = Medeba; Ya'zer = Jazer; Edre'i = Edrei; Ra'meses = Rameses; Sukkot = Succoth; Etam = Etham; Pi-haChirot = Pi-hahiroth; haChirot = Hahiroth; Baal-Tzefon = Baal-zephon; Migdol = Migdol; Dofqah = Dophkah; Alush = Alush; Refidim = Rephidim; Qivrot-haTa'avah = Kibroth-hattaavah; Chatzerot = Hazeroth; Ritmah = Rithmah; Rimmon-Peretz = Rimmon-perez; Livnah = Libnah; Rissah = Rissah; Qehelatah = Kehelathah; Mount Shefer = mount Shepher; Charadah = Haradah; Maqhelot = Makheloth; Tachat = Tahath; Terach = Terah; Mitqah = Mithkah; Chashmonah = Hashmonah; Moserot = Moseroth; Benei-Ya'aqan = Bene-jaakan; Chor-haGidgad = Hor-haggidgad; Yotvatah = Jotbathah; Avronah = Abronah; Etzyon-Gever = Ezion-geber; Tzin = Zin; Qadesh = Kadesh; Tzalmonah = Zalmonah; Punon = Punon; Dibon-Gad = Dibon-gad; Almon-Divlatayim = Almon-diblathaim; Avarim = Abarim; Nevo = Nebo; Yarden = Jordan; Yericho = Jericho; Beit-haYeshimot = Beth-jeshimoth; Avel-haShittim = Abel-shittim; Baal-Pe'or = Baal-peor; Beit-Pe'or = Beth-peor; Betzer = Bezer; Ramot = Ramoth; Gil'ad = Gilead; Re'uvenites = Reubenites; Menashites = Manassites; Aro'er = Aroer; Si'on = Sion; Chermon = Hermon; the Aravah = the Arabah.
entries.rationale: The Torah volumes continue the narrative Hebrew of genesis-woh, which transliterates names (Avraham, Ya'aqov, Yosef, Beit-El), and exodus-woh, whose signed-off chapters print 'Yisra'el', 'Aharon', 'Yehoshua', 'Refidim', 'Pi-haChirot' and 'Baal-Tzefon' but keep 'Moses' and 'Pharaoh' in English. Within one book a single practice must hold, and the signed-off exodus-woh chapters are not retro-edited; numbers-woh and deuteronomy-woh, which open in this wave, therefore adopt the exodus-woh practice so that the three Torah volumes read as one, including its two English exceptions. The Kings overlays transliterate 'Moshe' and 'Par'oh' and write 'Mitzrayim' with tz (ratified at the Kings sign-off, 2026-11-01), and describe exodus-woh's 'Moses' and 'Pharaoh' as a grandfathered single-book exception: the corpus therefore has two practices for these three names, which this entry records for the founder rather than resolving by retro-editing either set of signed-off chapters. For tsade the Torah volumes already print tz in names (Yitzchaq, Baal-Tzefon, genesis-woh Etzer), which agrees with the Kings rule, and keep ts only in 'Mitsrayim', the form fixed by the central entry. The equivalence table lets a reader match every form to the ASV and to the English editions of the Raëlian books, which quote these chapters with the KJV names (identical to the ASV forms in the table); the ASV form is also given in commentary at the first occurrence of each new name in a chapter. The Mitsrayim / 'the Egyptians' rule describes exodus-woh's published practice (3:9 miṣrayim lōḥăṣîm 'the Egyptians are oppressing'; Ex 14 passim) and departs from the central entry's gentilic 'Mitsri'; the departure is recorded in the central diff of this wave as a corpus note. The convention carries no interpretive content. Ratified at human sign-off (2026-11-01, zarazinsfuss): the Torah volumes keep the published exodus-woh forms ('Moses', 'Pharaoh', 'Mitsrayim', 'the Egyptians'); the split with the Kings forms stays recorded for a later corpus normalization pass.

entries.lemma: Quotation marks for direct speech in the Torah volumes
entries.partOfSpeech: Presentation convention (shared Torah convention, identical in the three overlays)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: no quotation marks; NJPS / NRSV: double quotation marks, with the Deuteronomic discourses of Moses usually printed without outer marks (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: Double quotation marks for direct speech; single marks for speech within speech (as exodus-woh). Quoted poems and book-citations take double marks (Num 21:14-15 the Book of the Wars of YHWH; 21:17-18 the song of the well; 21:27-30 the Cheshbon song). Deuteronomy: the discourses of Moses are printed without outer quotation marks; the first discourse opens at Deut 1:6 and runs to 4:40, so Deut 4:1-40 carries no outer marks, speech cited inside it takes double marks (4:6, 4:10), and the narrator's frame resumes at 4:41.
entries.rationale: Hebrew has no quotation marks, and the convention only has to make the speech structure clear and consistent. exodus-woh prints double marks with single marks for embedded speech (e.g. Ex 3:14-15), and the Torah volumes follow it. Deuteronomy is different in kind: chapters 1-30 are almost entirely Moses' first-person discourse, introduced by the narrator at 1:1-5 and resumed at 4:41-49, 4:44-5:1 and later headings; wrapping thirty chapters in quotation marks would leave the speech within the speech (Moses quoting YHWH or the people, 4:10) three levels deep, and NJPS and most commentaries print the discourses without outer marks. Since this wave translates Deut 4 before Deut 1-3, the chapter file opens inside the discourse; vv 1-40 are therefore printed without outer marks and the narrative frame of vv 41-49 is unmarked narration. The rule should be applied unchanged when Deut 1-3 and 5 are translated.

entries.lemma: Textual baseline for the Torah volumes
entries.partOfSpeech: Text-critical convention (shared Torah convention, identical in the three overlays; same policy as the Kings and Ezekiel overlays and the exodus-woh kes-yah entry)
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: MT with occasional silent adoption of versional readings (e.g. Deut 4:37 'their seed after them')
entries.wohChoice: Translate the MT consonantal text, vocalization, Qere and accent division; give the Ketiv, the extraordinary points and the readings of the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, the Targums, the Peshitta and the Vulgate in commentary. Wave T1 sites: Ex 24:10 'they saw the Elohim of Yisra'el' (LXX 'the place where the God of Israel stood'; Onqelos 'the glory of the God of Israel'); 24:11 'they beheld the Elohim' (LXX 'they appeared in the place of God'); Num 21:1 'the way of Atarim' (LXX, Targums, Peshitta, Vulgate 'the way of the spies'); 21:14 'Vahev in Sufah' (crux, kept as an unfinished fragment); 21:18 'And from the wilderness to Mattanah' (LXX 'and from the well'); 21:24 'was strong' (MT ʿaz; LXX 'Jazer'); 21:28 'the lords of the high places' (LXX 'it swallowed'); 21:30 ʾăšer with an extraordinary point (Sam, LXX 'fire'); 21:32 Qere 'and drove out' (Ketiv wyyrš); Num 33:8 'from before haChirot' (Sam, Peshitta, Vulgate 'from Pi-haChirot'); Deut 4:30 phrase division by the athnach on hāʾēlleh; 4:33 'the voice of the Elohim' (Sam, LXX add 'living', cf. 5:26); 4:37 'his seed after him' (Sam, LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate, ASV 'their seed after them'); 4:48 'Mount Si'on' (Peshitta 'Sirion', cf. 3:9).
entries.rationale: The Wheel of Heaven Translation translates the Masoretic Text and records the ancient versions in the apparatus rather than adopting them in the line; this is the policy of genesis-woh, of exodus-woh (kes-yah-vs-nes-yah at Ex 17:16) and of the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. At every wave-T1 site the MT gives a construable sense: 'they saw the Elohim of Yisra'el' is the Hebrew, which the LXX and the Targums soften for theological reasons (Propp, Exodus 19-40, AB 2A, 2006); 'his seed after him' at Deut 4:37 refers distributively to each of the fathers or to Avraham (Driver, Deuteronomy, ICC, 1895; Tigay, JPS Deuteronomy, 1996), while the plural of the versions is a harmonization with the plural 'your fathers'; and at Num 21:30 the Masoretes mark ʾăšer as doubtful with a dot (one of the ten puncta extraordinaria of the Torah, Sifre Num 69) but still read it. Where a versional reading is widely preferred by modern commentators (Num 21:1 'the spies'; 21:30 'fire'), the commentary says so. At Deut 4:30 the accents attach 'in the latter days' to the second half of the verse, and the line follows them, as the Kings overlay does at 2 Kgs 2:14. The Qere is translated and the Ketiv recorded, as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays.

entries.lemma: ʾĕlōhîm (plural form), with and without the article
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering convention for the referent and article of ʾĕlōhîm in the Torah volumes (shared Torah convention, identical in the three overlays; Torah counterpart of elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings)
entries.wohChoice: (1) YHWH referent: 'the Elohim', with or without the Hebrew article, in narrative and in direct speech (central elohim-as-translation; exodus-woh 3:4, 13:17, 20:1, 20:16): Ex 24:11, 13; Num 21:5; Deut 4:32, 33, 35, 39. (2) Construct with a possessor: 'YHWH your/our/my Elohim', 'the Elohim of Yisra'el', 'the Elohim of your fathers' (Ex 24:10; Deut 4 passim). (3) Non-YHWH referent: lower-case 'elohim' ('upon their elohim', Num 33:4; 'there you shall serve elohim, the work of human hands', Deut 4:28; exodus-woh 20:3, 20). (4) Generic class in a comparison: lower-case 'elohim' ('what great nation is there that has elohim so near to it', Deut 4:7; 'has any elohim ventured to go and take for himself a nation', Deut 4:34). (5) Bare ʾēl as a predicate: 'El' (see el-qanna-el-rachum-bare-el-predicate-deuteronomy).
entries.rationale: The central elohim-as-translation entry fixes the untranslated 'Elohim' and the narrative article, and exodus-woh applies the article to the YHWH referent both in narrative and in speech, whether or not the Hebrew has it; the Torah volumes keep that practice, which differs from the Kings overlay's clause (2) only at anarthrous predicates, none of which occurs in this wave. The capital/lower-case distinction for other referents follows exodus-woh at Ex 20:3, 20 ('other elohim', central elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus) and the Kings clause (4); it is an editorial device, since Hebrew script has no case. Clause (4) follows the referent principle of the Kings clause (5): at Deut 4:7 the comparison 'as YHWH our Elohim is' sets YHWH against the gods of other nations (the plural adjective qərōḇîm 'near' does not decide the point by itself, since plural attributives also stand with ʾĕlōhîm of YHWH, Deut 5:26; Josh 24:19; GKC §132h), and at 4:34 the question 'has ʾĕlōhîm ventured to take for himself a nation ... as YHWH your Elohim did for you' compares YHWH with any other deity, so that a capital would make the verse compare YHWH with himself (NRSV and NJPS 'any god' at 4:34; Tigay 1996; the ASV 'hath God assayed' takes the YHWH referent, which is recorded in commentary). At 4:33 the voice heard from the fire is the voice of the Sinai theophany, and the YHWH referent is kept with the ASV. Whether 4:35, 39 ('YHWH, he is the Elohim; there is none else') is monotheistic in the later sense or a superlative claim within a world of other elohim is not decided by the case and is recorded in commentary.

entries.lemma: nep̄eš 'throat, breath, life, living being, self'
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering-scope convention for nep̄eš in the Torah volumes (shared Torah convention; same rule as nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings and nefesh-scope-ezekiel)
entries.wohChoice: Idiomatic English, not 'soul': 'the people became impatient' for wattiqṣar nep̄eš-hāʿām (Num 21:4, literally 'the nefesh of the people grew short'); 'we loathe' for wənap̄šēnû qāṣâ (Num 21:5); 'guard yourself' for šəmōr nap̄šəḵā (Deut 4:9) and 'take good heed to yourselves' for nišmartem ... lənap̄šōṯêḵem (Deut 4:15); 'with all your heart and with all your being' for the Deuteronomic pair bəḵol-ləḇāḇəḵā ûḇəḵol-nap̄šeḵā (Deut 4:29, as 1 Kgs 2:4; 8:48). The transliteration 'nefesh' is reserved for passages that name the nep̄eš as the life-component that departs or returns (central tzet-nephesh-departure-at-death-formula).
entries.rationale: nep̄eš ranges from 'throat' and 'appetite' to 'life', 'living being' and 'self' (BDB; HALOT nep̄eš 1-9; H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 1974), and the central glossary already rejects the Platonic 'soul' for it (nefesh-chayah 'living being'). The Kings and Ezekiel overlays render its idiomatic uses by 'life', 'being' or a reflexive, and the Torah volumes adopt the same rule so that one lexeme has one policy across the corpus. qṣr nep̄eš 'to be short of nep̄eš' is an idiom of impatience or exasperation (Num 21:4; Judg 16:16; Zech 11:8), rendered 'became impatient' as in the ASV's own verb, NRSV and NJPS; in Num 21:5 nap̄šēnû is the speakers themselves ('we loathe', NJPS 'we have come to loathe'). The Deuteronomic pair at 4:29 takes 'being', the whole living self, as in 1 Kgs 2:4 (Alter's rendering of Deut 6:5), and the reflexive uses at 4:9, 15 are rendered as reflexives. exodus-woh 16:16 (signed off) prints 'according to the number of your souls' for nep̄āšôṯ 'persons'; that rendering predates the rule and is flagged for the next Exodus pass, not retro-edited.

entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering convention for ʿēḏûṯ as the designation of the tablets and of the objects that house them (shared by exodus-woh and numbers-woh)
entries.standardEnglish: the testimony (ASV lower case); the Pact (NJPS); the covenant (NRSV at Ex 25:16, 21)
entries.wohChoice: 'the Testimony' (capitalised) where hāʿēḏuṯ designates the tablets (Ex 25:16, 21, as exodus-woh 16:34) and in the titles 'the ark of the Testimony' (Ex 25:22) and 'the tent of the Testimony' (Num 18:2); lower-case 'testimonies' for the plural legal term ʿēḏōṯ (Deut 4:45).
entries.rationale: In the Priestly texts hāʿēḏuṯ is a technical name for the two tablets (Ex 25:16, 21; 31:18 'the two tablets of the Testimony'; 40:20), and by extension it names the ark and the tent that house them (Ex 25:22; 26:33; Num 1:50; 9:15; 17:22-23; 18:2) (BDB; Propp 2006). exodus-woh already prints the capitalised 'the Testimony' at 16:34, where the manna jar is placed 'before the Testimony', and the capital marks the technical sense against the ordinary noun. NJPS 'the Pact' and NRSV 'the covenant' interpret the word through its Akkadian cognate adê 'treaty stipulations'; the commentary records that reading, but the line keeps the established English term. The plural ʿēḏōṯ in the Deuteronomic series 'testimonies, statutes and ordinances' (Deut 4:45) is the ordinary legal noun and stays lower case.

entries.lemma: zār, participle of zwr 'be strange, other'
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering decision for zār in the cultic sense 'one not authorized' (Num 18:4, 7; cf. 1:51; 3:10, 38; 16:40 ET; Ex 29:33; 30:33; Lev 22:10-13)
entries.literal: one who is other / an outsider
entries.standardEnglish: a stranger (ASV); an outsider (NRSV, NJPS); a layman (some commentaries)
entries.rationale: zār means 'other, not belonging', and its reference depends on the group from which the person is excluded: a foreigner in some contexts (Isa 1:7; Obad 11), a non-family member (Deut 25:5), and in the Priestly sanctuary law anyone outside the authorized circle, here every non-Aaronide or non-Levite, Israelites included (Milgrom, Numbers, JPS, 1990, and Studies in Levitical Terminology, 1970; Levine, Numbers 1-20, AB 4A, 1993). The ASV 'stranger' carried that sense in older English, but a modern reader takes it as 'foreigner', which is not what Num 18 means: the immediately following verses forbid ordinary Israelites (bənê yiśrāʾēl, v 22) to approach. 'An outsider' is the rendering of NRSV and NJPS and keeps the relational sense of the Hebrew. It is distinct from gēr 'resident alien', which the corpus renders 'sojourner' or 'stranger' by context.

entries.lemma: ḥrm (Hiphil) 'devote irrevocably to YHWH, consecrate to destruction'; ḥērem 'what is so devoted'
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering decision for the ḥērem vocabulary in numbers-woh (Num 18:14; 21:2-3)
entries.literal: every devoted thing / I will devote (their cities) / Devotion (place name)
entries.standardEnglish: everything devoted (ASV Num 18:14); utterly destroy (ASV Num 21:2-3); Hormah; devote to destruction (joshua-woh overlay, Josh 6-10)
entries.wohChoice: 'every devoted thing' for ḥērem as consecrated property (Num 18:14); 'devote ... to destruction' for the Hiphil in war (Num 21:2 'I will devote their cities to destruction'; 21:3 'they devoted them and their cities to destruction'), aligned with the joshua-woh overlay herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua; the place name transliterated 'Chormah', unglossed, its wordplay with the verb visible in the line and explained in commentary
entries.rationale: ḥērem denotes property or persons withdrawn irrevocably from common use and made over to the deity, either as priestly property (Lev 27:21, 28; Num 18:14; Ezek 44:29) or, in war, by destruction (Num 21:2-3; Deut 7:2; 20:17; Josh 6-7; 1 Sam 15); the Moabite Mesha stele uses the same verb for Mesha's devotion of Nebo to Ashtar-Kemosh (line 17) (N. Lohfink, TDOT 5, 1986, s.v.; P. D. Stern, The Biblical Ḥerem, 1991; Milgrom 1990). English has no single word for both senses, so the line uses 'devoted thing' where the sense is consecrated property and 'devote ... to destruction' where it is destruction in war (NRSV 'utterly destroy'; NJPS 'proscribe'); both renderings keep the root 'devote' visible, so the link between 18:14, 21:2-3 and the place name Chormah can be followed in English, which the ASV's 'utterly destroy' hides. The Former Prophets wave renders the Hiphil the same way (joshua-woh herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua, Josh 6:17-21; 10:1-40). This rendering replaces the ASV 'utterly destroy' of the editor draft, at the Reviewer's request ratified at the human sign-off (2026-11-01). The place name ḥormâ (21:3) is a play on the verb of the same verse; under the Torah name convention it is transliterated without a parenthetical gloss because the text does not state the etymology in a causal clause; with 'devoted ... to destruction' in the line the wordplay is visible without one. The root recurs in the Former Prophets (Josh 6:17-18; 1 Sam 15), so this entry and the joshua-woh entry should be promoted to one central ḥērem entry at merge (isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban' to be reconciled at the same time).

entries.source: הַנְּחָשִׁים הַשְּׂרָפִים / שָׂרָף / נְחַשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת / נֵס
entries.translit: hannəḥāšîm haśśərāp̄îm / śārāp̄ / nəḥaš nəḥōšeṯ / nēs
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering decision for the serpent vocabulary of Num 21:6-9
entries.literal: the serpents, the burning ones / a burning one / a serpent of bronze / a pole
entries.standardEnglish: fiery serpents ... a fiery serpent ... a serpent of brass ... a standard (ASV); seraph serpents ... a seraph figure ... a copper serpent ... a standard (NJPS); poisonous serpents ... a poisonous serpent ... a serpent of bronze ... a pole (NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'fiery serpents' (v 6); 'a fiery serpent' (v 8, 'serpent' supplied, as the ASV, for the bare śārāp̄); 'the serpent' for the collective singular hannāḥāš (v 7); 'a serpent of bronze' (v 9, under nechoshet-bronze-copper-alloy-cross-corpus); 'a standard' for nēs (vv 8-9, ASV)
entries.rationale: śārāp̄ is formed from śrp 'burn' and is used of serpents in Num 21:6, 8; Deut 8:15 (nāḥāš śārāp̄) and of the 'flying śārāp̄' in Isa 14:29; 30:6, while the plural names the six-winged attendants of Isa 6:2, 6 (BDB; HALOT; K. R. Joines, 'Winged Serpents in Isaiah's Inaugural Vision', JBL 86, 1967). The 'burning' is usually explained by the inflammation of the bite or by the serpent's colour, and the uraeus, the rearing cobra of Egyptian royal iconography, is the usual iconographic comparison (Joines; Milgrom 1990; Levine, Numbers 21-36, AB 4B, 2000). The ASV 'fiery serpent(s)' keeps the root sense and the distinction from the plain nāḥāš; NJPS 'seraph' keeps the link with Isa 6 but reads as an angel class to a modern reader. At v 8, where the Hebrew has only śārāp̄, the ASV supplies 'serpent' and the line does the same, since v 9 identifies the object as a nāḥāš; the commentary records the bare noun. The Isaiah occurrences should be harmonized with this entry when that book's editorial decisions are made. nēs is a signal pole or standard (Isa 5:26; 11:12; exodus-woh 17:15 'YHWH-Nissi (YHWH is my banner)'); the ASV 'standard' is kept. The Raëlian canon's reading of the episode as serum injections (The Book Which Tells the Truth, ch. 3) is recorded only in a labelled reception note; the line renders the Hebrew nouns.

entries.lemma: the vocabulary of the priestly and Levitical dues in Num 18
entries.partOfSpeech: Cluster entry recording the ASV renderings kept in Num 18 and their modern alternatives (the offering terms proper are governed by the central qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus)
entries.literal: for anointing (or: as a portion) / a perpetual due / fat (= the best) / new wine / the first (part) / the first-ripe fruits / fire-offering (or: food-gift) / elevation-offering / covenant of salt / service of gift / curtain / wage
entries.standardEnglish: ASV: by reason of the anointing; a portion for ever; the best; the vintage; the first-fruits; the first-ripe fruits; an offering made by fire; wave-offering; a covenant of salt for ever; a service of gift; the veil; reward
entries.wohChoice: by reason of the anointing (v 8, ASV); a portion forever (vv 8, 11, 19); the best (vv 12, 29, 30, 32; literal 'fat' at v 17 of the sacrificial fat); new wine (v 12, for the ASV 'vintage'); the first-fruits of them (v 12) and the first-ripe fruits (v 13), kept distinct; an offering made by fire (v 17, ASV); wave-offering (vv 11, 18, ASV); a covenant of salt forever (v 19); a service of gift (v 7, ASV); the veil (v 7, ASV); your reward (v 31, ASV)
entries.rationale: Num 18 sets out the dues of the priests and Levites in technical terms, several of which are disputed; where the ASV is a defensible reading the line keeps it and the commentary gives the alternatives, so that the chapter changes only where the corpus has ruled (tərûmâ and the verb hērîm under the central qorbanot entry; zār under zar-outsider-cultic-numbers-18). ləmošḥâ (v 8) is either 'by reason of the anointing' (ASV; Rashi 'for greatness') or, from a homonym mšḥ II, 'as a portion, perquisite' (BDB mošḥâ II; NJPS 'as a perquisite'; NRSV 'as a portion'); both have support and the ASV is kept. ʾiššeh (v 17) is traditionally derived from ʾēš 'fire', but the word is used of offerings that are not burned and is compared with Ugaritic iṯt 'gift' (Milgrom, Leviticus 1-16, 1991: 'food gift'); the ASV 'offering made by fire' is kept and the alternative recorded. tənûp̄â 'wave-offering' is a dedication rite whose motion is debated (Milgrom 'elevation offering'); the ASV is kept. ḥēleḇ 'fat' is used figuratively for the choicest part (vv 12, 29-32; Gen 45:18; Ps 81:17 ET 81:16), while v 17 has the literal sacrificial fat. rēʾšîṯ (v 12) and bikkûrîm (v 13) are different dues, the processed first portion and the first-ripe produce (Milgrom 1990), and keep different English words. bərîṯ melaḥ (v 19; Lev 2:13; 2 Chr 13:5) is an idiom of permanence and is rendered literally. śāḵār (v 31) is payment for work; the ASV 'reward' is kept and 'wage' given in commentary. pārōḵeṯ is the curtain before the most holy place; the ASV 'veil' is kept.

entries.lemma: maśkîṯ 'carved figure, image'; ṣelem 'image'; massēḵâ 'cast metal (image)'; bāmâ 'high place, cultic platform'
entries.partOfSpeech: Rendering decision for the cultic objects of Num 33:52
entries.literal: their carved figures / the images of their castings / their high places
entries.standardEnglish: their figured [stones] ... their molten images ... their high places (ASV); their figured objects ... their molten images ... their cult places (NJPS); their figured stones ... their cast idols ... their high places (NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'their figured stones ... their molten images ... their high places' (ASV, the bracketed 'stones' printed without brackets, as Lev 26:1 ʾeḇen maśkîṯ)
entries.rationale: maśkîṯ is a carved or figured object, and in cultic contexts specifically a carved stone, as the full phrase ʾeḇen maśkîṯ 'figured stone' shows (Lev 26:1; HALOT); the ASV supplies 'stones' in brackets and the line prints it as part of the rendering, as NRSV does. ṣalmê massēḵōṯām is literally 'the images of their castings', i.e. cast-metal images; 'molten images' (ASV) gives the sense. bāmâ is a raised cultic platform or shrine, and 'high places' is the established English term, kept by NRSV and used in the Kings chapters; NJPS 'cult places' is recorded. The decision is lexical. The Raëlian canon cites vv 52-53 as the destruction of the idols of the primitive tribes on the creators' advice (The Book Which Tells the Truth, ch. 3); that reading is recorded only in a labelled reception note.

entries.source: הָרוּחַ אֲשֶׁר עָלֶיךָ ; כְּנוֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם הָרוּחַ ; אֶת־רוּחוֹ ; וְרוּחַ נָסַע מֵאֵת יְהוָה
entries.translit: hārûaḥ ʾăšer ʿāleyḵā ; kənôaḥ ʿălêhem hārûaḥ ; ʾeṯ-rûḥô ; wərûaḥ nāsaʿ mēʾēṯ YHWH
entries.literal: the spirit that is upon you; when the spirit rested upon them; his spirit; and a wind set out from YHWH
entries.standardEnglish: the Spirit (ASV, capitalised; 11:17, 25, 26, 29); a wind (ASV 11:31); the spirit (NRSV, NJPS, lower case)
entries.wohChoice: lower-case 'spirit' for the rûaḥ that rests on Moses and is apportioned to the seventy elders, and for YHWH's rûaḥ that Moses wishes on all the people ('some of the spirit that is upon you', 11:17; 'took some of the spirit that was upon him ... when the spirit rested upon them', 11:25; 11:26; 'that YHWH would put his spirit upon them', 11:29); 'wind' for the physical wind that brings the quail (11:31). No capital 'Spirit'; the Kings transliteration 'ruach' is not extended to the Torah.
entries.rationale: Wave MC, Hebrew part (Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5). rûaḥ covers wind, breath and spirit (BDB; HALOT rûaḥ). The ASV's capital 'Spirit' reads the later doctrine of a personal Holy Spirit into a text that does not specify it, and NRSV and NJPS print lower case. The Torah volumes have so far rendered rûaḥ in a person as lower-case 'spirit' (genesis-woh 41:38 'a man in whom the spirit of Elohim is'; 45:27), with the one transliteration 'breath of Elohim' reserved for the cosmic rûaḥ of Gen 1:2 (central ruach-elohim), and the Isaiah and Latter-Prophets overlays do the same; the Kings and Former Prophets overlays transliterate 'ruach' where the rûaḥ acts on a person (1 Kgs 22:21-24; 2 Kgs 2:9, 15-16; Judg 6:34; 13:25). Num 11 is the Torah's chief text for a rûaḥ that is transferred from one bearer to others (ʾāṣal 'withdraw, set aside a portion', 11:17, 25) and produces prophetic behaviour, and 2 Kgs 2:9, 15 ('the ruach of Eliyahu rests on Elisha') is its closest parallel; the Torah rendering is kept so that the Torah volumes read alike, and the divergence from Kings is recorded for the founder in the wave report. The physical wind of 11:31 is the same noun and is rendered 'wind' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS); the commentary points out the link the Hebrew makes between the rûaḥ on the elders and the rûaḥ that brings the quail (Milgrom, JPS Numbers, 1990; Levine, Numbers 1-20, AB 4, 1993). The entry is direct: lower-case 'spirit' and 'wind' are the renderings of the major modern versions.

entries.literal: Burning; our nefesh is dry; the moisture/cake of the oil; the nurse (masc.); my evil; and they did not add; from his youth; about two cubits on the face of the ground; before it was cut off
entries.standardEnglish: Taberah; our soul is dried away; fresh oil; a nursing-father; my wretchedness; but they did so no more; one of his chosen men; about two cubits above the face of the earth; ere it was chewed (ASV)
entries.wohChoice: 11:3 'Tav'erah (Burning)' (new name, glossed under the Torah causal-clause rule; ASV 'Taberah'); 11:6 'our appetite is dried up' (nefesh-scope-torah; ASV 'soul'); 11:8 'the taste of fresh oil' (ASV; LXX 'a cake made with oil' and NJPS 'rich cream' in commentary); 11:12 'a nursing father' (masculine ʾōmēn); 11:15 'my wretchedness' (MT; the tiqqun soferim 'your evil' in commentary); 11:25 'but they did not do so again' (MT yāsāp̄û; versions 'they did not cease'); 11:28 'the attendant of Moses from his youth' (mibbəḥurāyw, from bəḥurîm 'youth'; ASV 'one of his chosen men'); 11:31 'about two cubits above the face of the ground' (central eretz, ground clause); 11:33 'before it was chewed' (ASV).
entries.rationale: Wave MC, Hebrew part (Editor pass 2026-11-02, claude-opus-5-5). Most of these sites keep the ASV and record the alternatives. Two need a ruling. (1) 11:28 mibbəḥurāyw: the vocalisation (shewa under the bet, qibbuts in the second syllable) is that of the abstract plural bəḥurîm 'youth, young manhood' (BDB s.v. bəḥurîm), not of baḥûrîm 'young men, chosen men', which would carry a full vowel under the bet; NJPS ('Moses' attendant from his youth') and ESV read it so, and the line follows the MT vocalisation against the ASV's 'one of his chosen men', which is reported in commentary. Ex 33:11 calls Yehoshua a naʿar 'young man' and Moses' attendant, which fits the MT. (2) 11:8 ləšaḏ haššāmen is uncertain (ləšaḏ elsewhere only Ps 32:4 'my vigour/moisture'); the ASV 'fresh oil' takes it as 'the juice/moisture of oil', the LXX enkris ex elaiou as a cake made with oil (cf. Ex 16:31 'wafers with honey'), NJPS as 'rich cream'; the ASV is kept, since no reading is certain and the canon's 'a delicacy made with oil', which follows the LXX tradition through the French Bible, is reported in commentary (Milgrom, JPS Numbers, 1990; Levine, Numbers 1-20, AB 4, 1993; Ashley, The Book of Numbers, NICOT, 1993). The tiqqun at 11:15 is listed among the tiqqunê sôp̄ᵊrîm (Mekhilta on Ex 15:7; Masorah), and the MT is translated as at Gen 18:22 (central tiqun-soferim-yhwh-stood-before-abraham). Tav'erah is a new form for the Torah name table (to be added when the shared Torah entry is next extended); it is glossed because v 3 states its etymology in a causal clause (kî-ḇāʿărâ), as Qivrot-haTa'avah at v 34. The entry is direct.
